We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

**Purpose and access.** “The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel identified by name and role in a roster approved in writing by the design owner. The parties may update the roster by email. Each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement before receiving access. The testing house remains responsible for their compliance. The testing house may not use the drawings, geometry or materials derived from them to develop, or help anyone else develop, a competing product.”

**Working copies and fixtures.** “The testing house may make the working copies reasonably needed for the tests, provided each copy is encrypted in storage and in transit and accessible only to approved personnel. It may derive only the geometry needed to design and make test fixtures for this engagement. The same access limits apply to fixture files and physical fixtures.”

**Destruction and verification.** “Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the engagement, the testing house must securely erase the drawings, working copies and derivative files and destroy the physical fixtures. It may retain test results and reports that do not disclose or permit reconstruction of the CAD geometry. Within the same period, it must provide a certificate from an independent verifier bound by confidentiality, identifying the categories of material destroyed, the destruction dates and methods, and any exceptions. A certificate accounting for all such material satisfies the verification requirement without a site visit.”

Can your backup system meet the 30-day deadline? If it requires a longer rotation, please propose a maximum expiry period for inaccessible encrypted backups and wording for how the verifier would confirm their final deletion.

Thank you for this constructive framework. Moving away from a blanket ban on copies and unannounced on-demand site audits addresses two of our major operational hurdles, particularly given that we operate a multi-client facility where unannounced third-party entry is prohibited.

To make this work operationally and satisfy our laboratory accreditation rules, we need to adjust a few mechanics regarding our specialist subcontractors, how we verify deletion, and our mandatory record-keeping. 

1. **Subcontractors vs. Individual Rosters:** We use a specialist machining shop to fabricate the test fixtures and an accredited partner lab for certain test phases. Managing an individual name-by-name roster across external shops is impractical, and we need a clear mechanism to substitute a specialist entity mid-project if scheduling or equipment issues arise. However, we can protect your IP by isolating *only* the mounting/interface extracts—never the full actuator assembly or internal CAD—before sending anything to a specialist.
2. **Calibration Records:** Under our accreditation standards, we are legally required to retain test and calibration records for two years. We can ensure these records are stripped of all CAD geometry and interface dimensions.
3. **Verification & Backups:** Bringing an external "independent verifier" into our secure IT environment and shared client areas creates confidentiality conflicts with our other customers. Instead, we propose a formal written attestation signed by a corporate officer (along with destruction certificates from our subcontractors). Regarding backups, our encrypted disaster-recovery snapshots rotate on a **90-day** cycle. Rather than having an external auditor inspect backup servers later, our officer can attest at the 30-day mark that live files are purged and backups are isolated, or deliver a supplemental attestation at Day 95 confirming the backup cycle has overwritten them.
4. ** Audit Fallback:** Just in case a certificate is incomplete and a site check is ever strictly required, we should specify advance notice and confidentiality boundaries so our other clients' test bays remain protected.

Here is our proposed markup to your text, including an attachment structure for the approved entities:

***

**Purpose, access and subcontractors.** “The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Internal access is limited to testing house personnel with a strict need to know. The testing house may also share isolated drawing extracts and derived fixture geometry (excluding full actuator assemblies or internal mechanisms) with the approved specialist machining shop and accredited laboratory listed in **Attachment A**. If the testing house needs to substitute or add a specialist during the engagement, it may propose a replacement by email; approval by the design owner will not be unreasonably withheld and will be deemed granted if no written objection is received within 3 business days. Every individual and subcontractor receiving access must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement before receiving access, and the testing house remains responsible for their compliance. Neither the testing house nor its subcontractors may use the drawings, geometry or derived materials to develop, or help anyone else develop, a competing product.”

**Working copies and fixtures.** “The testing house and its approved subcontractors may make the working copies reasonably needed for the tests and fixture fabrication, provided each digital copy is encrypted in storage and in transit and accessible only to authorized personnel. Only the minimum interface geometry needed to design, machine and mount test fixtures may be extracted or shared with subcontractors. The same access and confidentiality limits apply to fixture files and physical fixtures.”

**Destruction, retention and verification.** “Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the engagement, the testing house must (and must cause its subcontractors to) securely erase all live drawings, working copies, isolated extracts and derivative files, and scrap or destroy the physical fixtures. Routine encrypted system backups that cannot feasibly be selectively purged must remain inaccessible to operational users and be automatically overwritten within **90 days** after report acceptance or termination. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the testing house and its accredited laboratory may retain test results, reports and mandatory calibration records for **two years** (or as required by accreditation standards), provided they do not contain or permit reconstruction of the drawings or CAD geometry. 

Within the initial 30-day period, an authorized officer of the testing house must provide a signed written attestation (**Attachment B** format) confirming the destruction dates, methods and categories of live materials and physical fixtures destroyed (including subcontractor confirmations), and confirming that any remaining copies reside solely in inaccessible encrypted backups scheduled for overwrite within 90 days, followed by an email confirmation once the 90-day overwrite cycle completes. Timely delivery of complete attestations satisfies verification without a site inspection. If a material discrepancy in an attestation requires verification, the parties will agree on a remote document review or, if strictly necessary, a scoped audit of relevant administrative records on at least 10 business days’ written notice during normal hours, excluding physical access to shared or third-party client testing areas.”

***

Let us know if the isolated-extract safeguard and officer attestation (backed by Attachment A and Attachment B) work for your team, or if you want to refine the substitution approval window or Attachment details.

We can accept specialist access to isolated extracts and an officer’s attestation backed by subcontractor certificates. To keep staffing changes workable, we propose approving a pool of named alternates at the outset. We can also accept remote review as the first step if a certificate needs verification.

**Attachment A — personnel and substitutions.** “Attachment A lists each approved individual by name, employer and role, and identifies the materials each role may access. The design owner may approve alternates in advance. The testing house may switch between approved individuals within their listed roles without further approval and must revoke access promptly when an individual leaves the assignment. For a new individual or specialist entity, the testing house may submit the same details by email. The design owner will respond within three business days and will not unreasonably withhold approval. Access may begin only on express written approval, including by email. Before access, each recipient must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house remains responsible for each recipient’s compliance.”

The machining shop and partner lab may receive only the mounting or interface extracts and fixture geometry each needs for its listed task. Full assemblies and internal CAD stay with named testing house personnel. We accept your working-copy language and competing-product restriction.

**Retained records.** “The testing house and accredited partner lab may retain test results, reports and required calibration records for two years, provided the retained records omit all CAD geometry and interface dimensions and do not permit reconstruction of either. A longer mandatory period applies only to the affected records. The testing house must identify the applicable requirement and retention period to the design owner in writing. Each holder must securely erase its retained records when that period ends.”

**Attachment B — destruction and backups.** “All deadlines run from written acceptance of the final report or earlier termination. By day 30, an authorized officer must certify the dates, methods and categories of live material and physical fixtures destroyed, attach signed destruction certificates from each specialist that received material, and identify any outstanding exception. The certificate must identify any residual encrypted disaster-recovery backups and their scheduled expiry. Those backups must remain isolated from operational users and expire by day 90. If a disaster recovery requires restoration, the holder must erase protected material before releasing the restored system to operational users. By day 95, the officer must provide a signed supplemental attestation confirming actual expiry across all holders, supported by their confirmations, and identifying any exception and its corrective action.” One certificate suffices if the officer can confirm complete destruction, including backups, by day 30.

We accept your 10-business-day notice period and shared-area exclusions. For a material discrepancy, either party may request remote review of relevant redacted records. If that leaves the discrepancy unresolved, the design owner may require a review of the relevant administrative records by a mutually agreed independent reviewer bound by confidentiality, during normal hours and subject to those notice and access limits. The reviewer may report only findings relevant to the discrepancy.

Can you populate Attachment A with the proposed personnel and alternates for all three organizations and confirm that both specialists can support the day-30 and day-95 certifications?

We accept your wording on Retained Records, Attachment B (destruction and backups), and the tiered remote/independent administrative review for material discrepancies. Both our specialist machining shop and our accredited partner lab have confirmed they can meet the Day-30 live erasure/fixture destruction and Day-90 backup expiry (with signed certificates supporting our Day-30 and Day-95 attestations). In fact, the machining shop uses isolated local workstations without cloud backup for client G-code, so they will typically certify 100% final deletion at Day 30.

On **Attachment A**, we can populate named individuals and alternates for our internal team and the accredited lab's test leads, as well as the engineering/CAM leads at the machining shop. However, we want to flag two small operational details to ensure we stay strictly compliant during execution:

1. **Shop-floor/calibration technicians:** At the machining shop and partner lab, once the named lead engineer/manager generates the CNC toolpaths or mounts the physical fixture, shift machinists or metrology technicians interact with the physical fixture on the machine bed or shaker table, though they never access the CAD files or drawing extracts. Listing every shift operator by name creates constant roster churn. Can we distinguish between *digital extract access* (strictly named individuals + alternates) and *supervised physical fixture handling* (authorized shop/lab technicians under the direct supervision of a named lead)?
2. **Pre-approved backup entity & substitution timing:** Express email approval (without deemed approval) works fine for adding an individual, provided we also pre-approve a backup machining shop in Attachment A now, or commit that the 3-business-day turnaround is a firm SLA so a sudden spindle failure at Shop 1 doesn't stall your vibration test schedule waiting on an inbox.

Here is a slight refinement to your **Attachment A** clause to address shop-floor fixture handling, followed by the populated **Attachment A** template and **Attachment B** checklist structure for your review:

***

**Attachment A — personnel, entities and substitutions.** “Attachment A lists each approved organization and each approved individual by name, employer and role, and identifies the materials each role may access. The design owner may approve alternate individuals and backup specialist entities in advance in Attachment A. The testing house may switch between pre-approved individuals or pre-approved backup entities within their listed roles without further approval (notifying the design owner by email if activating a backup entity) and must revoke access promptly when an individual or entity leaves the assignment. Shop-floor machinists and calibration technicians employed by an approved organization who do not access digital drawings or extracts may handle physical fixtures under the direct supervision of a named lead on Attachment A, subject to the same written confidentiality obligations. For a new individual or specialist entity not listed in Attachment A, the testing house may submit the required details by email. The design owner will respond within three business days and will not unreasonably withhold approval; access for new additions may begin only on express written approval, including by email. Before access, each recipient must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house remains responsible for each recipient’s compliance.”

***

### Draft Attachment A: Approved Organizations, Personnel & Access Matrix

**1. Testing House (Lead Contractor)**
* **Permitted Materials:** Full actuator drawings, internal/assembly CAD geometry, derived interface extracts, fixture files, and physical fixtures.
* **Approved Personnel:**
  * *Lead Test Engineer:* [Name 1] | *Alternate:* [Name 2]
  * *CAD / Fixture Extraction Engineer:* [Name 3] | *Alternate:* [Name 4]
  * *Vibration Lab Manager / Certifying Officer:* [Name 5] | *Alternate:* [Name 6]

**2. Specialist Machining Shop**
* **Primary Entity:** [Precision Fixture Works LLC] | **Pre-Approved Backup Entity:** [Apex Aero Machining Inc.] *(activated only upon email notice if Primary has capacity/equipment downtime)*
* **Permitted Materials:** Isolated mounting/interface drawing extracts, derived fixture CAD/CAM files, and physical fixtures ONLY. (No full actuator assemblies or internal CAD).
* **Approved Personnel (Digital & Engineering Access):**
  * *Primary — Manufacturing / CAM Lead:* [Name 7] | *Alternate:* [Name 8]
  * *Primary — Quality / Inspection Lead:* [Name 9] | *Alternate:* [Name 10]
  * *Backup Entity — CAM Lead:* [Name 11] | *Alternate:* [Name 12]
  * *(Supervised shop-floor CNC operators/inspectors: physical fixture handling only; no CAD/drawing file access).*

**3. Accredited Partner Laboratory (ISO/IEC 17025)**
* **Approved Entity:** [MetroDynamics Calibration & Test Lab]
* **Permitted Materials:** Isolated mounting/interface extracts (only as needed to verify fixture/shaker coupling), physical fixtures, and non-geometric test/calibration data. (No full actuator assemblies or internal CAD).
* **Approved Personnel:**
  * *Lead Dynamics Engineer:* [Name 13] | *Alternate:* [Name 14]
  * *Quality & Calibration Manager:* [Name 15] | *Alternate:* [Name 16]
  * *(Supervised calibration/shaker technicians: physical setup and sensor calibration only; no CAD/drawing file access).*

***

### Draft Attachment B: Destruction & Backup Attestation Elements
To make sure our Day-30 and Day-95 certificates hit every point your team expects without friction, we propose Attachment B require the following fields:
1. **Engagement Reference & Trigger Date** (Date of written final report acceptance or termination).
2. **Inventory of Purged Live Material** (Categories covered: full CAD/drawings, isolated extracts, CAM/G-code files, working copies; erasure standard used, e.g., NIST SP 800-88 Purge/Clear; completion dates).
3. **Physical Fixture Disposition** (Method of physical destruction/scrapping—e.g., CNC milling/cutting of mounting interfaces prior to metal recycling—and date completed).
4. **Subcontractor Certificates Attached** (Signed confirmations from Machining Shop and Accredited Lab covering items 2 & 3).
5. **Retained Records Notice** (Confirmation that 2-year retained test/calibration records under ISO/IEC 17025 contain zero CAD geometry or interface dimensions; citation of any longer statutory/accreditation rule if applicable).
6. **Encrypted Backup Status** (Confirmation of isolation from operational users, restoration-scrubbing protocol in place, and exact scheduled overwrite date ≤ Day 90; followed by Day-95 supplemental sign-off confirming final overwrite across all holders).

***

Does the supervised shop-floor carve-out for physical fixtures—paired with pre-approving the backup machine shop in Attachment A—work for your side? If so, we can plug in the specific staff names once we finalize the clause text.

Yes. We accept supervised physical fixture handling and advance approval of a backup machining shop. We propose the following wording for the technician exception in Attachment A.

“An approved machining shop or partner laboratory may assign its employees to handle a physical fixture for fabrication, inspection, setup or calibration under the direct supervision of a lead named in Attachment A. Before handling the fixture, each technician must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The named lead must control access to drawings, extracts, CAD/CAM files and toolpaths. A supervised technician may operate a machine running a program loaded by the named lead. Only named personnel may view, retrieve, edit or copy the program or its geometry. Technicians may take measurements needed for the assigned task. Only named personnel may retain or export dimensional records, which are subject to the agreed destruction requirements. Personnel who conduct the vibration tests or access drawing extracts must be named in Attachment A.”

We accept your backup-shop activation wording. Please fill in the legal entity names, leads and alternates, identify the materials each role needs, and confirm that the backup shop can meet the same destruction and certification deadlines. **Our written approval of the completed Attachment A will pre-approve the listed backup shop and its named personnel.** After that, the testing house may activate the backup by email notice before transferring any material. The notice should identify the work being transferred. Each shop that received material must account for its own copies and fixtures, even if its assignment ended before report acceptance.

We accept the Attachment B checklist with the agreed requirement that each attestation identify any outstanding exception and corrective action. A single day-30 attestation closes verification if it confirms complete destruction across all holders, including backups. Otherwise, the signed day-95 supplement is due. The populated Attachment A is the remaining item for approval before access begins.

We accept your exact wording for the supervised technician exception, the backup-shop activation notice (identifying the transferred work prior to transfer), the requirement that any shop receiving material provide destruction certifications even if its assignment ends early, and the Attachment B exception/corrective-action tracking.

We have also verified with our backup machining shop (**Apex Aero Machining Inc.**) that they use an air-gapped local CAM server with a 30-day encrypted snapshot cycle, and they have confirmed in writing that they will meet the exact same confidentiality, toolpath-control, Day-30 live/fixture destruction, and backup certification deadlines.

Below is the fully populated **Attachment A** (incorporating our named vibration test conductors so all personnel running the tests are explicitly listed) along with the consolidated **Attachment B** form structure for your written approval.

***

### Attachment A: Approved Organizations, Personnel & Access Matrix

**1. Testing House (Lead Contractor): Dynamics Test Partners Inc.**
* *Vibration Lab Manager & Certifying Officer:* Elena Rostova | *Alternate:* Marcus Vance
  * **Permitted Materials:** Full actuator drawings, assembly/internal CAD geometry, derived interface extracts, fixture CAD/CAM files, dimensional inspection records, and physical fixtures (for oversight, audit, and destruction verification).
* *CAD & Fixture Extraction Lead:* David Chen | *Alternate:* Priya Nair
  * **Permitted Materials:** Full actuator drawings and assembly/internal CAD geometry (solely to isolate mounting interfaces), derived interface extracts, and fixture CAD files.
* *Vibration Test Engineer (Conducting Tests):* Samuel Okafor | *Alternates:* Hannah Lindqvist, Carlos Mendez
  * **Permitted Materials:** Full actuator drawings (reference during test execution), isolated interface extracts, physical fixtures, test articles, and vibration test profiles/data.

**2. Primary Specialist Machining Shop: Precision Fixture Works LLC**
* *Manufacturing & CAM Lead:* Robert Kowalski | *Alternate:* Jenna Sterling
  * **Permitted Materials:** Isolated mounting/interface drawing extracts, derived fixture CAD/CAM files, CNC toolpaths, and physical fixtures. *(No full actuator assemblies or internal CAD).*
* *Quality & Dimensional Inspection Lead:* Thomas Cho | *Alternate:* Rachel Alvarez
  * **Permitted Materials:** Isolated mounting/interface drawing extracts, dimensional inspection records (to be purged by Day 30), and physical fixtures. *(No full actuator assemblies or internal CAD).*
* *Supervised Shop-Floor Personnel:* Employed CNC operators and metrology technicians operating under the direct supervision of the named leads per the supervised-technician clause (physical fixture handling, running lead-loaded machine programs, and task measurements only; zero access to view, retrieve, edit, or copy CAD/CAM files, extracts, or dimensional exports).

**3. Pre-Approved Backup Machining Shop: Apex Aero Machining Inc.**
*(Activated only upon prior email notice to Design Owner identifying the specific work being transferred; bound to full Day-30/Day-95 certification even if assignment ends early).*
* *Manufacturing & CAM Lead:* Gregory Mercer | *Alternate:* Diane Takahashi
  * **Permitted Materials:** Isolated mounting/interface drawing extracts, derived fixture CAD/CAM files, CNC toolpaths, and physical fixtures. *(No full actuator assemblies or internal CAD).*
* *Quality & Inspection Lead:* Kevin Patel | *Alternate:* Sarah Jenkins
  * **Permitted Materials:** Isolated mounting/interface drawing extracts, dimensional inspection records (to be purged by Day 30), and physical fixtures. *(No full actuator assemblies or internal CAD).*
* *Supervised Shop-Floor Personnel:* Same strict limits and lead supervision as Primary Machining Shop.

**4. Accredited Partner Laboratory (ISO/IEC 17025): MetroDynamics Calibration & Test Lab LLC**
* *Lead Dynamics Engineer (Conducting Partner-Phase Vibration Tests):* Dr. Aris Thorne | *Alternates:* Megan Brooks, Liam O’Connor
  * **Permitted Materials:** Isolated mounting/interface extracts (for shaker/fixture coupling verification), physical fixtures, test articles, and vibration test data. *(No full actuator assemblies or internal CAD).*
* *Quality & Calibration Manager:* Rebecca Lin | *Alternate:* Victor Alvarez
  * **Permitted Materials:** Physical fixtures (for setup/mass-loading calibration) and non-geometric calibration/test records. *(No CAD geometry or drawing extracts).*
* *Supervised Lab Technicians:* Employed calibration and setup technicians operating under the direct supervision of the named leads per the supervised-technician clause (physical fixture setup and sensor calibration only; does not conduct the vibration tests or access drawing extracts).

***

### Attachment B: Destruction & Backup Certification Checklist

**Part 1 — Day-30 Officer Attestation (Due ≤ 30 days from written report acceptance or earlier termination)**
Signed by Certifying Officer of Dynamics Test Partners Inc., attesting to and attaching:
1. **Trigger Event & Date:** Date of written acceptance of final test report or termination.
2. **Live Digital Erasure:** Categories erased (full drawings/CAD, isolated extracts, fixture CAD/CAM, CNC toolpaths, dimensional inspection records, working copies), erasure method (e.g., NIST SP 800-88 Purge/Clear), and completion dates.
3. **Physical Fixture Destruction:** Method used to render mounting interfaces unusable and scrap fixtures (e.g., milling/cutting critical interfaces prior to recycling) and completion date.
4. **Subcontractor Certificates:** Attached signed destruction certificates from every approved specialist organization that received any protected material or physical fixture (including any shop whose assignment ended prior to report acceptance).
5. **Retained Records Confirmation:** Confirmation that retained test reports, results, and mandatory 2-year ISO/IEC 17025 calibration records omit all CAD geometry and interface dimensions and do not permit reconstruction of either (identifying in writing any specific record subject to a longer mandatory accreditation/legal retention period and its scheduled erasure date).
6. **Backup Status:** Either (a) confirmation that all backups across all holders have also been permanently purged as of Day 30 (closing verification), OR (b) identification of any residual encrypted disaster-recovery backups across Dynamics Test Partners Inc. and its specialists, confirming operational isolation, restoration-scrubbing controls, and scheduled overwrite dates on or before Day 90.
7. **Exceptions & Corrective Action:** Explicit statement of "None," or detailed description of any outstanding exception and the specific corrective action and timeline.

**Part 2 — Day-95 Supplemental Officer Attestation (Required if backups remained at Day 30; due ≤ Day 95)**
Signed by Certifying Officer of Dynamics Test Partners Inc., supported by written confirmations from each relevant specialist holder, confirming:
1. **Backup Expiry:** Actual completion dates of the overwrite/expiry of all encrypted backups across all holders on or before Day 90.
2. **Exceptions & Corrective Action:** Explicit statement of "None," or identification of any exception and its completed or active corrective action.

***

Please confirm if you approve the completed Attachment A and Attachment B, and we will consider the replacement clauses and schedules finalized.

The design owner approves the completed Attachment A and Attachment B as submitted. This message constitutes written approval of the listed organizations, named personnel, alternates and role-specific access limits, including advance approval of Apex Aero Machining Inc. under the agreed prior email notice requirement.

The agreed replacement clauses and both attachments are final.
